chunks: My father narrated to us (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hamid narrated to us from the one who narrated to him, who said:

A man from the family of Abu Talib died, and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had not attended him. A group of people came, and when he sat down, the people held back as if birds were on their heads, and they were recalling poverty and death. When he sat down, he began by saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Between sixty and seventy is the battleground of deaths.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Poverty is the trial of Islam.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet and Imam al-Hasan say about the significance of the age 60-70 and the nature of poverty in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this narration highlights the Imam's presence in the absence of the Prophet, emphasizing the continuity of authority within the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam's citation of the 'battleground of deaths' underscores the vulnerability of the elderly, while his declaration that 'poverty is the trial of Islam' identifies material deprivation as a primary test of faith and social justice, a theme frequently explored in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the purification of the believer.

en.basel-kadem: 65.	We were told by my father, and Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they both said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from Muqatil bin Sulayman, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:

When Musa, peace be upon him, climbed the mountain and silently called to his Lord, Exalted and Glorious is He, he said: O my Lord, show me Your treasures. He said: O Musa, My treasures is only that when I want something, I say to it: «Be» and it is.
